title: Module 2 assessment
subtitle: Workbooks, Data Entry & Formatting
description: Fifteen questions across the whole of Module 2. Every question explains its answer, right or wrong.

questions.question: You type `07-10` into a cell and Excel shows `07-Oct`. What happened?
options: Excel read it as a date and stored a serial number
questions.explanation: Excel recognises anything that looks like a date and converts it to a serial number counting days from 1 Jan 1900. The cell now holds a number, not your text - which is why 07-10 can come back as 7 October when you meant product code 07-10. Format the column as Text first.

questions.question: Changing a cell's number format changes the value stored underneath.
questions.explanation: Formatting changes only what you see. A cell showing 4 may hold 3.6 - and SUM adds the 3.6, not the 4, which is why a formatted column can appear not to add up. ROUND changes the value; formatting never does.

questions.question: Why do experienced users avoid Merge & Center?
options: It breaks sorting, filtering and many formulas
questions.explanation: A merged cell is one cell pretending to be several, so Excel refuses to sort or filter across it and references behave oddly. Center Across Selection, under Format Cells > Alignment, looks identical and breaks nothing.

questions.question: A1 contains `Jan`. You drag its fill handle down four cells. What appears in A3?
questions.explanation: AutoFill recognises built-in lists - months, weekdays - and continues the series rather than copying. You can add your own under File > Options > Advanced > Edit Custom Lists, which is how to make a department or branch order fill automatically.

questions.question: You type 1 in A1 and 2 in A2, select both, then drag down. What does A5 contain?
questions.explanation: Two cells establish the step, so Excel continues 3, 4, 5. With one cell selected it would simply copy. This is also how to build any arithmetic series - 5, 10 gives you fifteens and twenties.

questions.question: Your report prints across nine pages and column headers appear only on page one. What do you set?
options: Rows to repeat at top, under Page Setup > Sheet
questions.explanation: Freeze Panes is a screen feature and has no effect on print. Page Setup > Sheet > Rows to repeat at top prints the header row on every page - the difference between a report people can read and one they put down.

questions.question: Deleting a worksheet can be undone with Ctrl+Z.
questions.explanation: Sheet deletion is one of the few actions Excel cannot undo - it clears the undo stack entirely. Right-click > Move or Copy to a backup workbook before deleting anything you might want back.

questions.question: A column of amounts must show as 1,250 and also feed a SUM. Custom number format, or TEXT()?
options: TEXT() - it gives exact control over the display
Custom number format - the cell keeps a real number
questions.explanation: TEXT() returns text, and text does not add up - SUM would return 0. Format the cell when the value must stay numeric; reserve TEXT() for joining a number into a sentence, where text is what you actually want.

questions.question: A column of numbers imported from a system is left-aligned by default and will not SUM. What is the most likely cause?
options: They are stored as text, not numbers
questions.explanation: Excel right-aligns numbers and left-aligns text by default, so alignment is a free diagnostic. ISNUMBER confirms it, and Text to Columns with Finish is the quickest bulk fix.

questions.question: Which number format shows a negative value in red with brackets?
options: A custom format with a section after the first semicolon
questions.explanation: A custom format has up to four sections separated by semicolons: positive;negative;zero;text. `#,##0;[Red](#,##0)` handles the first two. Knowing the semicolon structure unlocks most of what custom formats can do.

questions.question: To put the same entry into every selected cell at once, you type it and press Enter.
questions.explanation: Enter commits to one cell and moves on; Ctrl+Enter is the one that fills the whole selection. Select the range, type once, press Ctrl+Enter - the entry lands in all of them, with formula references adjusting per cell. It is the fastest way to fill a filtered or scattered selection where dragging will not work.

questions.question: A colleague's sheet uses eight colours, four fonts and three border styles, and nobody can see the numbers that matter. What is the fix?
options: More colour to highlight the key figures
Remove formatting until only meaning-bearing emphasis remains
questions.explanation: Formatting is a signal, and signal only works against a quiet background. If everything is emphasised, nothing is. One accent colour used consistently beats eight used decoratively.

questions.question: Your report is one column too wide for the page. Which Page Setup option fixes it without shrinking everything?
options: Fit to 1 page wide by 1 tall
Fit to 1 page wide, leaving the height automatic
questions.explanation: Setting width to 1 page and leaving height blank keeps the scale readable and lets the report run to as many pages as it needs. Forcing 1 by 1 on a long report shrinks it to the point of uselessness.

questions.question: What does right-clicking a sheet tab and choosing Move or Copy with 'Create a copy' ticked do?
options: Creates a link to the sheet
Duplicates the sheet, including its formulas and formatting
questions.explanation: It duplicates everything, and formulas pointing within the sheet re-point to the copy. It is the safe way to experiment - work on the duplicate and the original is untouched if you are wrong.

questions.question: A date and a time can be stored in the same cell as one number.
questions.explanation: The whole number is the day and the decimal is the fraction of a day, so 45200.75 is a date at 6pm. That is why you can subtract one timestamp from another and get a sensible duration.
